decisions.reason: The approved Hero V remains the unchanged reference geometry; the source changes only how the second V is proportionally derived from it.
The source does not change the E/L architectural design language; its cap-height scaling clause is already owned by the separate E/L cap-height Requirement.
The source describes the second V's natural right-arm overhang but does not change the locked terminal relationship between the Hero V and É accent.
The source does not alter the requirement that the É accent be literally derived from the approved Hero V terminal.
The source reiterates the existing hierarchy in which the E/L height follows the second V's left arm and only its right arm extends above them; it does not change that candidate state.
The source does not discuss or alter the shared peak alignment between the Hero V and É accent.
The source postpones further spacing evaluation until the second-V hierarchy is established but does not change the selected kerning or spacing rules.
The source restates the existing rule that E and L height aligns with the second V's left arm; the proportional change to the reference glyph does not invalidate or modify that relational rule.
The source contains design instructions but does not change the obligation to explain design rationale with review rounds.
The source does not change the established common-baseline alignment rule.
The second-V proportional-scaling decision has no necessary effect on the deferred champagne material treatment.
